# Data Source: stripe_treasury_transaction

A change to the balance of a Treasury financial account, made by one money movement. It lives on a connected account, so read it through a provider configuration whose `stripe_account` is that account. Look one up by its `id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "connected_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "The connected account the object lives on."
}

provider "stripe" {
  alias          = "connected"
  stripe_account = var.connected_account
}

data "stripe_treasury_transaction" "deposit" {
  provider = stripe.connected
  id       = "trxn_1MtYCCLkdIwHu7ixgXzLiVq8"
}

output "transaction_flow_type" {
  value = data.stripe_treasury_transaction.deposit.flow_type
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the treasury transaction to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) transferred.
* `balance_impact` - Change to a FinancialAccount's balance See [`balance_impact`](#balance_impact) below.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount associated with this object.
* `flow` - ID of the flow that created the Transaction.
* `flow_details` - Details of the flow that created the Transaction. See [`flow_details`](#flow_details) below.
* `flow_type` - Type of the flow that created the Transaction. Possible values: `credit_reversal`, `debit_reversal`, `inbound_transfer`, `issuing_authorization`, `other`, `outbound_payment`, `outbound_transfer`, `received_credit`, `received_debit`.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `status` - Status of the Transaction. Possible values: `open`, `posted`, `void`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`status_transitions`](#status_transitions) below.

<a id="balance_impact"></a>
### `balance_impact`

The `balance_impact` attribute supports:

* `cash` - The change made to funds the user can spend right now.
* `inbound_pending` - The change made to funds that are not spendable yet, but will become available at a later time.
* `outbound_pending` - The change made to funds in the account, but not spendable because they are being held for pending outbound flows.

<a id="flow_details"></a>
### `flow_details`

The `flow_details` attribute supports:

* `credit_reversal` - You can reverse some [ReceivedCredits](https://docs.stripe.com/api#received_credits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedCredit leads to the creation of a new object known as a CreditReversal. See [`flow_details.credit_reversal`](#flow_details.credit_reversal) below.
* `debit_reversal` - You can reverse some [ReceivedDebits](https://docs.stripe.com/api#received_debits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedDebit leads to the creation of a new object known as a DebitReversal. See [`flow_details.debit_reversal`](#flow_details.debit_reversal) below.
* `inbound_transfer` - Use [InboundTransfers](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/into/inbound-transfers) to add funds to your [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts) via a PaymentMethod that is owned by you. The funds will be transferred via an ACH debit. Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using InboundTransfer objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/into/inbound-transfers) See [`flow_details.inbound_transfer`](#flow_details.inbound_transfer) below.
* `issuing_authorization` - When an [issued card](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing) is used to make a purchase, an Issuing `Authorization` object is created. [Authorizations](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/purchases/authorizations) must be approved for the purchase to be completed successfully. Related guide: [Issued card authorizations](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/purchases/authorizations) See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization) below.
* `outbound_payment` - Use [OutboundPayments](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-payments) to send funds to another party's external bank account or [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts). To send money to an account belonging to the same user, use an [OutboundTransfer](https://docs.stripe.com/api#outbound_transfers). Simulate OutboundPayment state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_payments` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects. Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using OutboundPayment objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-payments) See [`flow_details.outbound_payment`](#flow_details.outbound_payment) below.
* `outbound_transfer` - Use [OutboundTransfers](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-transfers) to transfer funds from a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts) to a PaymentMethod belonging to the same entity. To send funds to a different party, use [OutboundPayments](https://docs.stripe.com/api#outbound_payments) instead. You can send funds over ACH rails or through a domestic wire transfer to a user's own external bank account. Simulate OutboundTransfer state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_transfers` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects. Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using OutboundTransfer objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-transfers) See [`flow_details.outbound_transfer`](#flow_details.outbound_transfer) below.
* `received_credit` - ReceivedCredits represent funds sent to a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts) (for example, via ACH or wire). These money movements are not initiated from the FinancialAccount. See [`flow_details.received_credit`](#flow_details.received_credit) below.
* `received_debit` - ReceivedDebits represent funds pulled from a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts). These are not initiated from the FinancialAccount. See [`flow_details.received_debit`](#flow_details.received_debit) below.
* `type` - Type of the flow that created the Transaction. Set to the same value as `flow_type`. Possible values: `credit_reversal`, `debit_reversal`, `inbound_transfer`, `issuing_authorization`, `other`, `outbound_payment`, `outbound_transfer`, `received_credit`, `received_debit`.

<a id="flow_details.credit_reversal"></a>
### `flow_details.credit_reversal`

The `flow_details.credit_reversal` attribute holds a treasury credit reversal, with the attributes of the [`stripe_treasury_credit_reversal`](../data-sources/treasury_credit_reversal) data source and `object`, the name of its type.

<a id="status_transitions"></a>
### `status_transitions`

The `status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `posted_at` - Timestamp describing when the Transaction changed status to `posted`.
* `void_at` - Timestamp describing when the Transaction changed status to `void`.
